cands.name: Tracy Clark
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 57 (Northern Greensboro) since August 2024, when she was appointed to finish Ashton Clemmons's term. Previously head of marketing and a board member at a wealth management firm, with 15+ years in marketing. President of Women 2 Women Greensboro.

endorsements.text: Her 2024 Ballotpedia survey lists these endorsements, which are self-reported: Planned Parenthood Votes South Atlantic, Moms Demand Action, Everytown for Gun Safety, and the North Carolina Association of Educators.
For 2026, Ballotpedia lists a voter guide recommendation from Waves of Democracy (a Sway voting group run by Terri Robinson).

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Tracy Clark on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration enforcement or H-1B, or police pay and pensions. Her campaign site lists Community Safety, Housing and Economic Development as priorities, but we could only read the home and About pages, not those issue pages. We did not see a specific statement from her on teacher raises or on school choice funding. We could not confirm details of the bills she sponsored. The Wikipedia page for her has no content beyond one sentence. We found no controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements beyond those listed. 'Moved' does not apply, since she was born and raised in North Carolina.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Asheville and says she graduated from Brevard High School, and her campaign site says she was born and raised in North Carolina.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since August 2024. Before that she was head of marketing and a board member at a 75-employee NC wealth management firm that was sold to Modera Wealth Management, with 15+ years in marketing in financial services, technology and online media. She also has an MBA/MSIS from UNC.
qual.why: One term of actual legislative service plus business management experience places her in the upper-middle range. Her nonprofit presidency, board seat and fellowship were not counted. She has no law, policy or budget career on record.
qual.label: One term of actual legislative service plus business management experience places her in the upper-middle range. Her nonprofit presidency, board seat and fellowship were not counted. She has no law, policy or budget career on record.

second-amendment.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said the first bill she would introduce is a revival of House Bill 525, allowing law enforcement or a 'concerned citizen' to petition for Extreme Risk Protection Orders (red-flag orders) to temporarily bar a person from having a firearm.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she criticized the 12-week abortion limit and listed reproductive freedom among her top policy priorities. She also said she would like a ballot initiative process so North Carolinians could vote on reproductive access.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she criticized state politicians for diverting public tax dollars to 'unregulated, scam-ridden private school usage.' Her campaign site also criticizes private school vouchers for wealthy families, though it does not name a specific voucher bill. In the same survey she said NC teachers are significantly underpaid.
